keyframe_review.note: 684 km2 for 1188-1235: the Boulonnais around Boulogne-sur-Mer, two grid cells, inside the Flanders shape in 1187. The page gives no area and no extent ('centred on the city of Boulogne-sur-Mer'). The shape also covers 1212-1223 when the page has the county merged into Artois and then under Philip Hurepel; the county stayed an entity, so no change is drawn.

New keyframe for 1236-1240, where Cliopatria has no Boulogne row and draws the cells inside the Kingdom of Portugal: the page has Matilda II 'continued to reign' after Philip Hurepel's death in 1235 and marry Alphonse of Portugal in 1238, so the county continued. The 1241 shape is carried back.
640 km2 for 1241-1249 (-6%): outline noise; Matilda II and Alphonse of Portugal hold the county (1238-1253). No event in the pages opened explains the change. Unverified: page budget.

640 km2 for 1250-1259: unchanged. Alphonse divorced Matilda in 1253 and she kept the county; the row ends in 1259 and the county passes to the Counts of Auvergne (ledger merge). Cliopatria has no Boulogne shape 1260-1476; the Boulonnais lies inside the County of Auvergne shape to 1470.

ledger.note: 1188: Cliopatria's County of Boulogne row begins; the page is silent on a founding. It says the county has 'few records prior to the 11th century', 'seems to have come under the rule of the counts of Flanders in the late 9th or early 10th century' (infobox 'acquisition by the House of Flanders: 896') and that Eustace II sailed with William the Conqueror 'in 1066': the county is older than the row. Cliopatria draws the Boulonnais inside the Flanders shape in 1187.
1190: Renaud of Dammartin becomes Count of Boulogne. The page dates his Boulogne tenure from 1190; in 1191 his father Alberic 'kidnapped and had Dammartin marry Ida, Countess of Boulogne'.

1212: Philip II takes the county into the royal hands. 'It was merged into the County of Artois by Philip II of France in 1212' (the page does not say confiscation; the Renaud page has Philip seize Renaud's lands in 1211 after he refused to appear in a suit). The Boulonnais stays a county: Cliopatria keeps its shape, and the next holder is Philip Hurepel.

1214: after Bouvines the county goes to the king's son Philip Hurepel. Renaud joined the attack that culminated at the Battle of Bouvines, commanding the Brabançons, and was one of the last to surrender (paraphrase); 'His county was granted to Philip's illegitimate son, Philip Hurepel.' The County page has Hurepel count jure uxoris only on his marriage to Matilda II in 1223: the pages differ on whether the grant was 1214 or 1223.

1223: 'Boulogne passed under nominal royal control in 1223', when 'Philip Hurepel became count jure uxoris upon his marriage to Matilda II' (Renaud's daughter). He revolted against Blanche of Castile in 1226 and died in 1235, after which Matilda continued to reign.

1238: Matilda II marries Alphonse, second son of Alfonso II of Portugal (king as Afonso III from 1248; he divorced her in 1253). Cliopatria draws the Boulonnais inside the Kingdom of Portugal shape in 1236 and 1240.

1259: the county passes to the Counts of Auvergne. After Matilda it 'passed to Matilda's niece, Adelaide of Brabant' and her husband William X of Auvergne; the page gives no year, so 1259 is Cliopatria's last year for the Boulogne row. Cliopatria draws the Boulonnais inside the County of Auvergne shape from 1260 to 1470 (2 of 2 cells); the county is dormant as a separate state until 1477.

1437: 'Bertrand V de la Tour succeeded to the counties of Auvergne and of Boulogne in 1437.' In 1435 the Treaty of Arras made Boulogne a vassal of the Duke of Burgundy (Treaty of Arras page; recorded in the Duchy of Burgundy dossier).

1477: the county is incorporated into the royal domain. 'In 1477, Bertrand II dealt with Louis XI, exchanging the county of Boulogne with the county of Lauragais'; Boulogne 'became part of the royal domain' (infobox 'incorporation into the crown lands of France: 1477'). The War of the Burgundian Succession page has French forces seize Boulogne in the first months of 1477.

wars.name: Battle of Bouvines
wars.outcome: Renaud of Dammartin, Count of Boulogne, fought on the imperial side, was defeated by Philip II and held at Péronne until his death (1227); his county was granted to Philip Hurepel. No border moved.
wars.note: Renaud's lands had been seized in 1211 and he made an agreement with King John at Lambeth on 4 May 1212 (Renaud page); the County page says Boulogne was 'merged into the County of Artois' in 1212.

wars.name: War of the Burgundian Succession

zones.text: Boulogne, among the territories seized by French forces in the first months of 1477

wars.outcome: French forces seized Artois, Boulogne, Ponthieu and Vermandois in the first months of 1477; the County page has Bertrand II exchange Boulogne with Louis XI the same year.

certainty.note: A small fief with no boundary on any page; the outline is Cliopatria's two-cell shape.

notes:
Written for eu-10-e from two new pages (County of Boulogne, Renaud of Dammartin; budget 1-2) and two already opened for the Duchy of Burgundy dossier. Cliopatria's row is three small shapes 1188-1259 (684/640 km2); the pages give no area.
LIFE: the dossier runs 1188-1477. 1188 is Cliopatria's start and the page is silent on a founding (the county is older: under Flanders from the late 9th or early 10th century, Eustace II in 1066); the found event is confidence 1. 1477 is the page's incorporation into the royal domain. From 1259 to 1476 the county is a dormant span inside the County of Auvergne shape (gazetteer: the two Boulogne cells are covered by county-of-auvergne 1260-1470); the dossier records merge 1259 (confidence 1: the page gives no year for the passage to Adelaide of Brabant and William X of Auvergne) and has no keyframes then. The holders in between are not given years on the page (1259 to 1437) and no ruler strip is written.
PAGES DISAGREE: Philip Hurepel received the county in 1214 (Renaud page) or became count jure uxoris in 1223 (County page); the County page says it was 'merged into the County of Artois' in 1212 without saying confiscation, the Renaud page says Philip seized the lands in 1211. The ledger records these as holder changes (rename), not as loss and gain, because Cliopatria keeps the shape and the county stayed a county.
NOT DONE (page silent): 'In 1347 ... Calicas was annexed as a territory within the Kingdom of England' (County page) is not placed: the page does not say what Calicas is or that it lay in the county (Calais is a guess). The 1435 vassalage to the Duke of Burgundy (Treaty of Arras page) is recorded in the Duchy of Burgundy dossier, where it ends in 1477. Cliopatria draws the cells inside the Portugal shape in 1236-1240 (Alphonse of Portugal's marriage, 1238) and inside Auvergne from 1260; a gap-filler should check the 1236 start.
Gazetteer: no 'Boulonnais' or 'Boulogne-sur-Mer' entry; the region is drawn through the Cliopatria shape.
